notebooklm-mcp 1.0.8

# notebooklm-mcp v1.0.4

- Improved authentication guardrails, requiring explicit user consent for all cookie extraction and headless auth methods.
- Updated guidance to clarify browser-based login is the default and only allow OpenClaw CDP or manual cookie file with user confirmation.
- Expanded security and isolation best practices, including stricter deletion of cookie files and per-project auth cache recommendations.
- Removed the sample `skill-card.md` file.

notebooklm-mcp 1.0.3

- Added explicit triggers for skill activation when mentioned in English or Portuguese (see "When to use": supports both "use /notebooklm-mcp" and "execute notebooklm-mcp").
- Removed unused file: skill-card.md.

notebooklm-mcp 1.0.2 changelog

- Updated documentation in SKILL.md; improved skill instructions and descriptions.
- Removed the obsolete skill-card.md file.

notebooklm-mcp 1.0.1

- Updated security guardrails: now clarifies this is an unofficial client, and adds explicit steps requiring human confirmation for any browser cookie handling.
- Expanded and tightened guidance in SKILL.md on authentication, cookie safety, and install verification.
- Removed deprecated quickstart file (skill-card.md) to avoid duplication and security ambiguity.
- Improved instructions around manual and headless authentication scenarios.
- Emphasized never automating, reading, or forwarding credentials or cookies without explicit user instruction.

notebooklm-mcp 1.0.0 — Initial Release

- Introduces support for Google NotebookLM (Gemini Notebook) access via CLI (`nlm`) and MCP server (`notebooklm-mcp`).
- Documents step-by-step authentication on headless servers, including manual cookie extraction and OpenClaw CDP integration.
- Explains when and how to use the skill for diagnosing tool/listing/auth errors in MCP environments (e.g., Claude Code, Devin, Cursor, Gemini).
- Clarifies installation, guardrails (security, cookie handling), and protocol for troubleshooting common login/config issues.
- Not intended for MCP server development; focuses on user-facing configuration and authentication.
